Contract clause 5.1 requires Ibadan Starch Processing Ltd. to meet the quality_standard of Grade A starch content >= 18%. This standard applies to all deliveries made under the Agreement. Record status: current.

The starch content shall be measured by the laboratory of ISPL or an independent laboratory agreed by both parties, using the standard iodine titration method or an equivalent method acceptable to both parties.

**2.2 Grade Classification**

| Grade | Starch Content (minimum) | Moisture Content (maximum) | Foreign Matter (maximum) | Fibre Content (maximum) |
|-------|--------------------------|----------------------------|--------------------------|--------------------------|
| Grade A | 18% | 12% | 1% | 3% |
| Grade B | 15% | 13% | 2% | 4% |
| Grade C | 12% | 14% | 3% | 5% |

Only Grade A cassava shall be delivered under the Agreement, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both parties.

**2.3 Testing Procedures**

Testing shall be carried out at the point of delivery at ISPL's processing facility in Ibadan. Samples shall be taken from each delivery in accordance with the sampling procedure set out in Schedule 3.

The results of the tests shall be recorded in the delivery docket and signed by both the representative of OSCGF and the representative of ISPL. Any dispute as to the quality of a delivery shall be referred to an independent laboratory for testing. The cost of the independent test shall be borne by the party whose test result is found to be incorrect.

**2.4 Rejection of Substandard Deliveries**

If a delivery fails to meet the Grade A standard, ISPL may reject the delivery or accept it at a reduced price to be agreed between the parties. If the parties cannot agree on a reduced price, the delivery shall be returned to OSCGF at OSCGF's cost.

SUBJECT: PROCESSING OF CHANGE REQUEST LAEL-CRF-2022-014

1.0 INTRODUCTION

This memo is to inform members that a change request form has been received from Lagos Agro-Exports Ltd. (LAEL), dated 2022-08-10. The form was logged into our registry on 11 August 2022 and assigned the internal tracking number above.

2.0 SUMMARY OF THE REQUEST

LAEL is requesting modifications to the supply agreements covering maize and sesame. Specifically, they seek to increase the monthly maize volume from 400 MT to 550 MT and to change the sesame delivery cadence from monthly to bi-weekly. The requested effective date for both changes is 01 September 2022.

3.0 REVIEW PROCESS

The Management Committee is requested to review the application under the following heads:

3.1 Volume Feasibility: The Secretariat has verified that the proposed maize volume increase is within the aggregate production forecast for the season, provided the Kwara cluster performs to at least 90% of its projected yield. Members are asked to confirm whether the Federation’s buffer stocks can accommodate the earlier drawdown.
| Item | Current Plan (MT) | With LAEL Increase (MT) | Variance |
|------|-------------------|--------------------------|----------|
| Total contracted maize volume (all offtakers) | 28,400 | 28,550 | +150 |
| Projected aggregate production (Kwara, Niger, Benue clusters) | 31,200 | 31,200 | 0 |
| Buffer stock requirement (10% of contracted) | 2,840 | 2,855 | +15 |
| Projected surplus after contractual commitments | 2,800 | 2,650 | -150 |

The revised offtake remains within the projected production envelope, provided the Kwara cluster achieves at least 90% of its projected yield of 12,400 MT. Should the Kwara cluster underperform, the Secretariat notes that drawdown from the Federation's strategic reserve may be required earlier than planned.

**4.0 LOGISTICS CONSIDERATIONS**

The additional 150 MT per month will require approximately 5 additional truckloads per month (based on 30 MT per truck). The Lagos corridor remains the primary evacuation route. The following constraints were identified:

- **Storage at Lagos port facility:** LAEL has confirmed available covered storage of 1,200 MT, sufficient to accommodate the increased volume with a 2-week buffer.
- **Weighbridge capacity at Ibadan central depot:** Current throughput is 85% of capacity during peak harvest months (Oct–Dec). An additional 150 MT per month adds approximately 3.5% to peak throughput, which remains within operational tolerance.
- **Transport availability:** The Transport and Logistics Unit has confirmed that contracted haulage capacity can absorb the additional movements without new procurement, subject to the current fuel supply situation.

**5.0 FINANCIAL IMPLICATIONS**

The volume increase will have the following financial effects:

- **Increased revenue to the Federation:** At the current indicative price of ₦285,000/MT, the additional 150 MT per month generates ₦42.75 million in monthly revenue, or ₦513 million annually.
- **Working capital requirement:** The Secretariat estimates an additional ₦38.4 million in working capital will be required to finance the incremental procurement, based on a 45-day procurement-to-delivery cycle.
- **No change to the price per tonne:** LAEL has not requested a price adjustment in connection with this volume increase. The existing price escalation clause in Agreement MAZ/LAEL/2021-03 remains applicable.

**6.0 RECOMMENDATION**

The Secretariat recommends that the Management Committee approve the volume increase, subject to the following conditions:

1. The Kwara cluster production forecast is confirmed at the next cluster coordination meeting (scheduled for 22 August 2022).
2. LAEL provides a revised offtake schedule and confirms its storage capacity in writing.
3. The Federation's buffer stock drawdown protocol is reviewed to ensure the earlier drawdown can be accommodated without jeopardising the strategic reserve minimum level.

The change request form from Lagos Agro-Exports Ltd. indicates a change_request_type of volume increase. Record status: current.

Members are invited to submit comments to the Secretariat by close of business on 18 August 2022.

**1.0 PROCUREMENT AND LOGISTICS**

1.1 The increase from 400 MT to 550 MT per month will require LAEL to expand its

- Gbagi Grain Link, Ilorin (registration no. KWC/AGG/2021-118)
- Niger Basin Commodities, Bida (registration no. NGS/AGG/2022-041)

1.3 The aggregators have confirmed, in writing, that they can supply the additional
volumes starting from September 2022 harvest. Their collection points are within
15 km of the existing LAEL intake depot in Ilorin, which will reduce transport
costs per tonne by approximately 4% compared to the current average.

**2.0 STORAGE AND HANDLING**

2.1 LAEL's current storage capacity at the Apapa facility is 2,300 MT, of which
approximately 1,800 MT is available for maize. The remaining 500 MT is used for
soya, sorghum, and bagged fertiliser.

2.2 To accommodate the increased monthly intake, LAEL will commission an additional
silo at the Ilorin depot. The silo has a capacity of 600 MT and is expected to be
operational by 15 September 2022. A copy of the commissioning schedule is attached
as Annex C.

2.3 In the interim, LAEL will lease covered warehouse space at the Ogun State
Agricultural Development Agency (OGSADA) complex in Abeokuta. The lease agreement

**4.0 FINANCING AND CASH FLOW**

4.1 The expanded procurement will require additional working capital of
approximately 85 million naira per month. LAEL has secured a facility from a
commercial bank to cover this requirement. The facility is a revolving credit line
with an interest rate of 16% per annum, secured against LAEL's export contract with

---

**SCHEDULE 2 – QUALITY STANDARDS AND ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA**

This Schedule forms part of the Supply Agreement. It sets out the quality standards applicable to all cassava supplied by OSCGF to ISPL under the Agreement.

**2.1 Quality Standard – Starch Content**

Contract clause 5.1 requires Ibadan Starch Processing Ltd. to meet the quality_standard of Grade A starch content >= 18%. This standard applies to all deliveries made under the Agreement. Record status: current.

The starch content shall be measured by the laboratory of ISPL or an independent laboratory agreed by both parties, using the standard iodine titration method or an equivalent method acceptable to both parties.

**2.2 Grade Classification**

| Grade | Starch Content (minimum) | Moisture Content (maximum) | Foreign Matter (maximum) | Fibre Content (maximum) |
|-------|--------------------------|----------------------------|--------------------------|--------------------------|
| Grade A | 18% | 12% | 1% | 3% |
| Grade B | 15% | 13% | 2% | 4% |
| Grade C | 12% | 14% | 3% | 5% |

Only Grade A cassava shall be delivered under the Agreement, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both parties.

**2.3 Testing Procedures**

Testing shall be carried out at the point of delivery at ISPL's processing facility in Ibadan. Samples shall be taken from each delivery in accordance with the sampling procedure set out in Schedule 3.

The results of the tests shall be recorded in the delivery docket and signed by both the representative of OSCGF and the representative of ISPL. Any dispute as to the quality of a delivery shall be referred to an independent laboratory for testing. The cost of the independent test shall be borne by the party whose test result is found to be incorrect.

**2.4 Rejection of Substandard Deliveries**

If a delivery fails to meet the Grade A standard, ISPL may reject the delivery or accept it at a reduced price to be agreed between the parties. If the parties cannot agree on a reduced price, the delivery shall be returned to OSCGF at OSCGF's cost.

---

**MEMORANDUM**

**To:** All Cooperative Members
**From:** Quality Control Officer, OSCGF
**Date:** 2021-04-02
**Subject:** Quality Testing Procedures for 2021 Season

Dear Members,

Following the signing of the Supply Agreement with ISPL, I wish to remind all members of the quality testing procedures that will apply to all deliveries for the 2021 season.

1. All cassava delivered to ISPL must meet Grade A standard, which requires a minimum starch content of 18%. This is a contractual requirement and cannot be waived by any individual member or the Cooperative office.

2. Samples will be taken from each delivery at the point of delivery. The sampling method is set out in Schedule 3 of the Agreement. Members are advised to familiarise themselves with this Schedule.

3. The starch content test will be carried out by ISPL's laboratory. Members may request a copy of the test results for their own records.

4. If a delivery is found to be below Grade A standard, the delivery may be rejected or accepted at a reduced price. Members should note that the Cooperative will not bear the cost of rejected deliveries caused by substandard cassava.

5. Members are advised to harvest cassava at the correct maturity (12 to 18 months) to ensure the starch content meets the required standard. Early harvesting is a common cause of low starch content.

1.0 INTRODUCTION

This memo is to inform members that a change request form has been received from Lagos Agro-Exports Ltd. (LAEL), dated 2022-08-10. The form was logged into our registry on 11 August 2022 and assigned the internal tracking number above.

2.0 SUMMARY OF THE REQUEST

LAEL is requesting modifications to the supply agreements covering maize and sesame. Specifically, they seek to increase the monthly maize volume from 400 MT to 550 MT and to change the sesame delivery cadence from monthly to bi-weekly. The requested effective date for both changes is 01 September 2022.

3.0 REVIEW PROCESS

The Management Committee is requested to review the application under the following heads:

3.1 Volume Feasibility: The Secretariat has verified that the proposed maize volume increase is within the aggregate production forecast for the season, provided the Kwara cluster performs to at least 90% of its projected yield. Members are asked to confirm whether the Federation’s buffer stocks can accommodate the earlier drawdown.

The revised offtake remains within the projected production envelope, provided the Kwara cluster achieves at least 90% of its projected yield of 12,400 MT. Should the Kwara cluster underperform, the Secretariat notes that drawdown from the Federation's strategic reserve may be required earlier than planned.

**4.0 LOGISTICS CONSIDERATIONS**

The additional 150 MT per month will require approximately 5 additional truckloads per month (based on 30 MT per truck). The Lagos corridor remains the primary evacuation route. The following constraints were identified:

- **Storage at Lagos port facility:** LAEL has confirmed available covered storage of 1,200 MT, sufficient to accommodate the increased volume with a 2-week buffer.
- **Weighbridge capacity at Ibadan central depot:** Current throughput is 85% of capacity during peak harvest months (Oct–Dec). An additional 150 MT per month adds approximately 3.5% to peak throughput, which remains within operational tolerance.
- **Transport availability:** The Transport and Logistics Unit has confirmed that contracted haulage capacity can absorb the additional movements without new procurement, subject to the current fuel supply situation.

**5.0 FINANCIAL IMPLICATIONS**

The volume increase will have the following financial effects:

- **Increased revenue to the Federation:** At the current indicative price of ₦285,000/MT, the additional 150 MT per month generates ₦42.75 million in monthly revenue, or ₦513 million annually.
- **Working capital requirement:** The Secretariat estimates an additional ₦38.4 million in working capital will be required to finance the incremental procurement, based on a 45-day procurement-to-delivery cycle.
- **No change to the price per tonne:** LAEL has not requested a price adjustment in connection with this volume increase. The existing price escalation clause in Agreement MAZ/LAEL/2021-03 remains applicable.

**6.0 RECOMMENDATION**

The Secretariat recommends that the Management Committee approve the volume increase, subject to the following conditions:

1. The Kwara cluster production forecast is confirmed at the next cluster coordination meeting (scheduled for 22 August 2022).
2. LAEL provides a revised offtake schedule and confirms its storage capacity in writing.
3. The Federation's buffer stock drawdown protocol is reviewed to ensure the earlier drawdown can be accommodated without jeopardising the strategic reserve minimum level.

**1.0 PROCUREMENT AND LOGISTICS**

1.1 The increase from 400 MT to 550 MT per month will require LAEL to expand its
procurement catchment area. At present, LAEL sources approximately 60% of its maize
from the Kwara cluster, 25% from the Niger State corridor, and 15% from the Oyo
State surplus markets. The additional 150 MT per month will be sourced primarily
from the Kwara cluster (an additional 90 MT) and the Niger corridor (an additional
60 MT).

1.2 LAEL has engaged two additional aggregators, both registered with the Federation,
to support the expanded procurement. The aggregators are:
- Gbagi Grain Link, Ilorin (registration no. KWC/AGG/2021-118)
- Niger Basin Commodities, Bida (registration no. NGS/AGG/2022-041)

1.3 The aggregators have confirmed, in writing, that they can supply the additional
volumes starting from September 2022 harvest. Their collection points are within
15 km of the existing LAEL intake depot in Ilorin, which will reduce transport
costs per tonne by approximately 4% compared to the current average.

**2.0 STORAGE AND HANDLING**

2.1 LAEL's current storage capacity at the Apapa facility is 2,300 MT, of which
approximately 1,800 MT is available for maize. The remaining 500 MT is used for
soya, sorghum, and bagged fertiliser.

2.2 To accommodate the increased monthly intake, LAEL will commission an additional
silo at the Ilorin depot. The silo has a capacity of 600 MT and is expected to be
operational by 15 September 2022. A copy of the commissioning schedule is attached
as Annex C.

2.3 In the interim, LAEL will lease covered warehouse space at the Ogun State
Agricultural Development Agency (OGSADA) complex in Abeokuta. The lease agreement
commences 1 September 2022 and provides 400 MT of covered storage. This is a
temporary arrangement pending the Ilorin silo commissioning.

**3.0 QUALITY CONTROL**

3.1 The expanded procurement will require additional quality testing at the intake
points. LAEL will deploy two additional field officers to the Kwara cluster and one
to the Niger corridor. These officers will conduct moisture content tests and
aflatoxin screening at the point of aggregation.

3.2 The Federation's quality standards, as set out in the Quality Assurance Manual
(QAM-2021), will continue to apply. LAEL confirms that all maize supplied under the
increased volume will meet the following parameters:
- Moisture content: not exceeding 14%
- Broken kernels: not exceeding 3%
- Foreign matter: not exceeding 1.5%
- Aflatoxin: not exceeding 10 ppb

3.3 LAEL will provide monthly quality reports to the Federation, to be submitted
within five working days of the end of each month. The reports will be in the
format prescribed in QAM-2021, Section 4.

**4.0 FINANCING AND CASH FLOW**

4.1 The expanded procurement will require additional working capital of
approximately 85 million naira per month. LAEL has secured a facility from a
commercial bank to cover this requirement. The facility is a revolving credit line
with an interest rate of 16% per annum, secured against LAEL's export contract with
the Netherlands buyer.

4.2 The credit line agreement is subject to the Federation's confirmation of the
volume increase. LAEL requests that the Federation issue the confirmation by
22 August 2022, to allow the bank to disburse funds by 1 September 2022.

4.3 LAEL will absorb the financing cost without passing it on to the Federation.
The price per tonne under Agreement MAZ/LAEL/2021-03 remains unchanged.
